name: First Forge Signed Steel

rarity.note: No magic whatsoever — craft so reliable it functions like a guarantee.

summary: Blades signed at Hallord's First Forge: the smith's clan-ring struck twice into the tang, the steel folded over deep-folk charcoal, and the whole sworn on the never-dying fire. Signed steel holds an edge through a campaign and never — in four thousand years of records — has one broken in honest use. There is no enchantment in it. There doesn't need to be.
origin: The Deep-Forging's traditions; continuous production since ~450 AS
current_whereabouts: Everywhere serious soldiers and honest judges are found; forgeries everywhere else.
properties: Two ring-marks in the tang match the smith's registered pair at Hallord
Warranty is real: a broken signed blade entitles the bearer to the smith's clan-ring as forfeit
Courts accept signed steel as proof of identity in lieu of witnesses
keepers: Sold by charter at the Surface Porch; the clans limit yearly output to keep the signature honest.
value_or_danger: Twenty crowns honest; two bits forged — and carrying a forgery insults every hold at once.
adventure_hooks: A signed blade breaks in honest use for the first time ever recorded; Hallord demands the pieces and the story.
Players must authenticate a dead man's blade before his clan will bury him — the rings say one thing, the widow another.
